test.title: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision - Test 1
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

A rubber ball is released from a height of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> above the floor. It bounces back repeatedly, always rising to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>81</mn><mn>100</mn></mfrac></math> of the height through which it falls. Find the average speed of the ball. (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

Soon after the collision, the particle comes to rest, and the atom recoils and goes to its first excited state. The initial kinetic energy of the particle (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>eV</mi></math>) is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>N</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>N</mi></math> is: (Given the mass of the hydrogen atom to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>GeV</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>).........

The position of the centre of mass of a uniform semi-circular wire of radius R placed in x-y plane with its centre at the origin and the line joining its ends as x-axis is given by, 0, xRπ. Then, the value of |x| is          .

A batsman hits back a ball of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> straight in the direction of the bowler without changing its initial speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The impulse imparted to the ball is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>.

A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> collides head on elastically with a stationary body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>. After collision, the smaller body reverses its direction of motion and moves with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The initial speed of the smaller body before collision is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

In a system two particles of masses $m_1=3 \mathrm{~kg}$ and $m_2=2 \mathrm{~kg}$ are placed at certain distance from each other. The particle of mass $m_1$ is moved towards the center of mass of the system through a distance $2 \mathrm{~cm}$. In order to keep the center of mass of the system at the original position, the particle of mass $m_2$ should move towards the center of mass by the distance _____ $\mathrm{cm}$.
